publications.title: A Formal Analysis of Agent Payment Protocols
publications.summary: Builds Tamarin models of x402, MPP, ACP and AP2 from their specifications, schemas and reference code using one shared abstraction of the agent payment lifecycle, then asks source-backed verification questions to expose missing bindings and cross-stage correspondences, which it consolidates into 18 security principles. Across 86 verification cases it reproduces 46 known or calibration cases, reports 40 new formal-consistency findings, and validates ten of them against x402 implementations through proofs of concept, SDK and schema witnesses and executable traces.
publications.whyItMatters: The only side-by-side formal model of x402, stripe-mpp, openai-acp and ap2 so far; it shows where each specification leaves delegated authority, settlement and fulfillment unbound.

publications.title: SoK: Security of Autonomous LLM Agents in Agentic Commerce
publications.summary: A systematization of knowledge that frames the security of autonomous LLM agents in commerce along five dimensions (agent integrity, transaction authorization, inter-agent trust, market manipulation, regulatory compliance), derives 12 cross-layer attack vectors from a curated corpus of papers, protocol documents, industry reports and incidents, and proposes a layered defense for the authorization gaps in current agent payment protocols. The ACP it lists is written 'Agent Commerce Protocol', which may not be OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol; that mapping is unconfirmed.
publications.whyItMatters: Places erc-8004, ap2, x402 and stripe-mpp in one threat framework and argues that their authorization gaps compound across the reasoning, tooling, custody and settlement layers.

publications.title: SoK: Blockchain Agent-to-Agent Payments
publications.summary: Systematizes blockchain-based agent-to-agent payments, with x402 as the lead example, into a four-stage lifecycle of discovery, authorization, execution and accounting, classifies representative designs at each stage, and isolates recurring weaknesses: weak intent binding, misuse under valid authorization, payment-service decoupling and limited accountability.
publications.whyItMatters: Gives a lifecycle vocabulary for x402 and for the discovery role that erc-8004 registries are meant to fill, and names the payment-service decoupling problem that later x402 attack papers exploit.

publications.title: Inter-Agent Trust Models: A Comparative Study of Brief, Claim, Proof, Stake, Reputation and Constraint in Agentic Web Protocol Design-A2A, AP2, ERC-8004, and Beyond
publications.summary: Compares six trust mechanisms for inter-agent protocols (brief, claim, proof, stake, reputation, constraint) and evaluates A2A, AP2 and ERC-8004 against them on security, privacy, cost and resistance to Sybil, collusion and whitewashing, with attention to LLM-specific weaknesses such as prompt injection and sycophancy. It argues that proof and stake should gate high-impact actions, with claims for discovery and reputation as an overlay. The arXiv record says it was submitted to the AAAI 2026 TrustAgent workshop; acceptance is not confirmed.
publications.whyItMatters: Direct comparative treatment of ap2 and erc-8004 trust assumptions; its warning that claim-only and reputation-only designs are brittle anticipates the empirical ERC-8004 Sybil findings.

publications.title: Can Trustless Agents Be Trusted? An Empirical Study of the ERC-8004 Decentralized AI Agent Ecosystem
publications.summary: First empirical study of ERC-8004 on Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Base from deployment through 2026-05-13, crawling Identity and Reputation Registry events, registration files and associated x402 payments. Only 3%, 4% and 15% of registrations on the three chains expose a valid registration file with a live endpoint, reputation values are not commensurable and are cheap to manipulate, and 73.5%, 59.2% and 90.6% of reviewers show coordinated Sybil behavior; removing flagged feedback leaves 15.8%, 77.9% and 86.8% of rated agents with no valid feedback.
publications.whyItMatters: Primary evidence for the disputed status of erc-8004 reputation data and for the gap between registrations and operational agents; it also links x402 settlements to registered identities.

publications.title: A dataset of early blockchain-registered AI agents on Ethereum
publications.summary: Describes a structured dataset of 10,000 ERC-8004 agents registered on Ethereum mainnet within a defined block range, combining on-chain identity records, minting and transfer events, reputation summaries and feedback records with resolved off-chain metadata, collected through Web3 RPC queries. The companion data are deposited on Harvard Dataverse under DOI 10.7910/DVN/HJZW8Q (a dataset DOI, which the arXiv record lists in place of a paper DOI).
publications.whyItMatters: A reusable baseline for erc-8004 measurement work; the Mafrur and Khusumanegara readiness study builds on data of this kind.

publications.title: From Agent Identity to Agent Economy: Measuring the Operational Readiness of ERC-8004 AI Agents
publications.venue: Journal of FinTech and Digital Assets, vol. 1, no. 2, pp. 69-88
publications.summary: Asks whether ERC-8004 agents on Ethereum are operationally ready beyond registration by building an agent-level feature table (identity status, metadata, service declarations, reputation feedback, transfers, cross-chain registration) and an evidence-layer readiness framework, complemented by network analysis of owner-agent, feedback-client and wallet-transfer graphs. Early adoption is registration-heavy but operationally shallow, and ownership and feedback activity are concentrated in a few wallets and clients.
publications.whyItMatters: Independent, journal-published measurement that supports the atlas distinction between erc-8004 identity registrations and a working agent economy.

publications.title: Five Attacks on x402 Agentic Payment Protocol
publications.summary: Formalizes x402 and demonstrates five practical attacks on authorization, binding, replay protection and web-layer handling, validated on local chains, Base Sepolia and live endpoints, plus an audit of three open-source SDKs and endpoints. The attacks yield either unpaid service or paid-but-denied outcomes, and the paper proposes mitigations.
publications.whyItMatters: Direct attack catalog for x402 that spans the HTTP layer and the on-chain settlement layer.

publications.title: When HTTP 402 Meets the Blockchain: Risks on Emerging x402 Payments
publications.summary: Studies facilitator-mediated x402 deployments in the wild, derives eight security rules for facilitators and four attack vectors (Free Shopping, Asset Theft, Service Denial, Gas Abuse), and applies a semi-automated black-box tool to 15 facilitators serving over 60,000 sellers and 360,000 buyers, finding violations in all of them. Findings were disclosed and mitigated, including changes by Coinbase, and the paper adds a measurement of more than 119 million Base and Solana transactions. Listed on the USENIX Security 2026 technical sessions page (accessed 2026-10-10).
publications.whyItMatters: Peer-reviewed evidence that the x402 facilitator is a shared trust point whose flaws affect many merchants at once, plus adoption and centralization metrics.

publications.title: Free-Riding the Agentic Web: A Systematic Security Analysis of x402 Payments
publications.summary: Analyzes x402 as a stack of HTTP semantics, per-chain schemes and SDK choices against five invariants and finds four flaw classes: cross-resource substitution, duplicate-settlement races, allowance overdraft and denial of settlement, reaching resource-leakage ratios up to 100% against official SDKs and a production deployment. It also proves that output-only pay-per-token pricing cannot be both fair and bounded against hidden reasoning-token inflation, and proposes mitigations with provable guarantees.
publications.whyItMatters: Explains the state-synchronization gap between synchronous HTTP and asynchronous settlement that is specific to x402-style rails.

publications.title: How Agentic Is Agentic Commerce? A Population-Scale Measurement of x402 Adoption and Authenticity
publications.summary: Population-scale measurement of x402 on Base over a 280-day window (136,708,672 settlements worth about 44.1 million dollars) with a coarser Solana census. Resolving the true payer through the meta-transaction layer, the authors classify 21.20% of settlements as fictitious and 63.78% as internal to a linked cluster, bound genuinely independent value between about 188 thousand and 20.3 million dollars, and conclude that the settlement count measures manufacturability rather than adoption.
publications.whyItMatters: The main source for the dispute over x402 volume authenticity; any x402 metric on the atlas should be shown alongside this analysis.

publications.title: A402: Binding Cryptocurrency Payments to Service Execution for Agentic Commerce
publications.summary: Proposes A402, a payment architecture that binds cryptocurrency payments to service execution through Atomic Service Channels and TEE-assisted adaptor signatures, so that payment finalizes only if the requested service is executed and delivered, with a TEE-based liquidity vault aggregating channel settlements on chain. Evaluated against x402 on Bitcoin and Ethereum integrations.
publications.whyItMatters: Addresses the end-to-end atomicity gap that x402 leaves open, and connects agent micropayments to the payment-channel lineage.

publications.title: Hardening x402: PII-Safe Agentic Payments via Pre-Execution Metadata Filtering
publications.summary: Presents presidio-hardened-x402, open-source middleware that intercepts x402 payment requests before transmission to redact personally identifiable information from payment metadata, enforce declarative spending policies and block replays. On a synthetic corpus of 2,000 metadata triples the recommended NLP mode reaches a micro-F1 near 0.9 at p99 latency under 6 ms; version 2 of the preprint revises the threshold and headline numbers.
publications.whyItMatters: Highlights that x402 metadata travels to facilitators that are typically not bound by data processing agreements, a privacy control gap in the protocol as deployed.

publications.title: Sybil-Resistant Service Discovery for Agent Economies
publications.summary: Introduces TraceRank, a reputation-weighted ranking for x402-enabled services in which payment transactions act as endorsements, seeded with precomputed reputation and propagated through the payment graph weighted by value and recency, then combined with semantic search. The authors argue that this resists Sybil spam because many low-reputation payers rank below a few high-reputation ones.
publications.whyItMatters: An early proposal for discovery and reputation over the x402 payment graph, the same problem that erc-8004 reputation registries target.

publications.title: Enhancing the A2A Protocol with Blockchain-Based Identities and x402 Micropayments for Agentic AI
publications.venue: IJCCI 2025, Springer Communications in Computer and Information Science (CCIS), pp. 454-472
publications.summary: Extends the A2A protocol with ledger-anchored identities, publishing AgentCards on chain as smart contracts for verifiable discovery, and with x402 micropayments so that agents can discover, authenticate and pay one another across organizational boundaries; includes an implementation and evaluation. Published in Springer CCIS from IJCCI 2025 under the title given here; the arXiv preprint (2507.19550, 2025) carries the longer title 'Towards Multi-Agent Economies: Enhancing the A2A Protocol with Ledger-Anchored Identities and x402 Micropayments for AI Agents'.
publications.whyItMatters: Peer-reviewed design that pairs x402 with on-chain agent identity, the same combination that erc-8004 plus x402 deployments pursue.

publications.title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
publications.summary: Systematic security analysis of AP2 v0.2 across five lifecycle phases and five deployment architectures, using MAESTRO threat modeling to catalog 48 threats in five families and AIVSS scoring to flag eight High-band threats, each demonstrated on a purpose-built testbed with proofs of concept and mitigations, plus a deployment-aware scanner. The central finding is that valid mandate signatures do not guarantee that a transaction reflects user intent when the pre-authorization context is manipulated.
publications.whyItMatters: Most complete threat catalog for ap2 to date, and it covers the A2A and MCP inputs that sit outside the signed mandates.

publications.title: Zero-Trust Runtime Verification for Agentic Payment Protocols: Mitigating Replay and Context-Binding Failures in AP2
publications.summary: Analyzes the AP2 mandate lifecycle and finds runtime enforcement gaps created by retries, concurrency and orchestration, then proposes a zero-trust runtime verifier that enforces explicit context binding and consume-once mandate semantics with time-bound nonces. Simulations at up to 10,000 transactions per second show both mechanisms are needed to stop replay and context-redirect attacks, at about 3.8 ms verification latency.
publications.whyItMatters: Shows that ap2 (and ucp, which it also names as a mandate-based protocol) needs execution-time checks on mandates, not just signature validity at issuance.

publications.title: Whispers of Wealth: A Systematic Red-Teaming Study of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
publications.venue: IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Multimedia, Networking, and Security (IMNS) 2026, pp. 1-6
publications.summary: Red-teams a working AP2 shopping agent built with Gemini 2.5 Flash and the Google ADK and introduces two prompt-injection techniques, the Branded Whisper Attack, which manipulates product ranking, and the Vault Whisper Attack, which extracts sensitive user data, showing that simple adversarial prompts reliably subvert agent behavior. The IEEE version carries the title given here; the arXiv preprint (2601.22569) is titled 'Whispers of Wealth: Red-Teaming Google's Agent Payments Protocol via Prompt Injection'.
publications.whyItMatters: First published attack paper on ap2 and the origin of the whisper-attack line that Louck and colleagues extend in 2026.

publications.title: Protocol-Level Attacks on Agentic Commerce Platforms: A Cross-Platform Taxonomy, AIP-Bench, and Unified Defense
publications.summary: Argues that the most consequential risks in agentic commerce platforms sit in the protocol between agents and commerce services rather than in the model, documenting 33 structural vulnerabilities across three platforms that succeed deterministically regardless of model, three of which chain into a payment hijack. Contributes a taxonomy, AIP-Bench as a deterministic benchmark, and PCAT, a platform-agnostic defense that removes four of five structural attack classes.
publications.whyItMatters: Cross-platform evidence that protocol design, not model alignment, decides the security of openai-acp, ap2 and ucp style checkout flows; the three platforms are not named in the abstract, so the mapping is unconfirmed.

publications.title: Issuer-Sovereign Agentic Payments
publications.summary: Proposes Issuer-Sovereign Agentic Payments, in which the cardholder approves a spending rule once with the issuing bank's own authentication component, and at payment time the bank checks the merchant against that rule and generates the card authentication value only if allowed, so the transaction rides normal card rails with issuer validation and no extra execution-time dependency.
publications.whyItMatters: A counterproposal to network-led designs such as visa-tap and mastercard-agent-pay, where spending controls are enforced by the network or a credential provider rather than the issuer.

publications.title: TessPay: Verify-then-Pay Infrastructure for Trusted Agentic Commerce
publications.summary: Introduces TessPay, a two-plane verify-then-pay infrastructure for agentic commerce: agents are anchored in a canonical registry and user intent is captured as verifiable mandates, funds are escrowed during execution while the agent produces cryptographic evidence (TLS Notary, TEE) for a Proof of Task Execution, settlement releases funds only when the evidence satisfies verification predicates, and a tamper-evident audit trail supports disputes.
publications.whyItMatters: Combines the mandate idea of ap2 with the registry and validation functions of erc-8004 into one escrow design; a useful comparison for how the protocols split those functions.

publications.title: Compliance-Aware Agentic Payments on Stablecoin Rails
publications.summary: Describes a compliance-aware architecture that combines x402-style signature-based payment authorization and relayed execution with programmable compliance enforced on chain through a policy wrapper and a policy manager coordinating modular checks, so settlement stays low-friction when conditions are met and transaction-linked attestations are recorded. The arXiv comment labels it a demo-track paper, but no venue is confirmed.
publications.whyItMatters: Shows one route to adding regulatory checks to x402 settlement at execution time rather than in an off-chain workflow.

publications.title: Visibility into AI Agents
publications.summary: Assesses three measures for visibility into AI agents, agent identifiers, real-time monitoring and activity logging, outlines implementations that vary in intrusiveness and informativeness, and analyzes how they apply across centralized and decentralized deployments, including implications for privacy and concentration of power.
publications.whyItMatters: Foundation for the agent identifier idea that visa-tap, erc-8004 and ap2 each implement in their own way.

publications.title: IDs for AI Systems
publications.summary: Proposes a framework in which IDs are ascribed to instances of AI systems, such as a particular agent session, with associated information accessible to parties that interact with them, and argues that demand for IDs is strongest where systems can make financial transactions or contact real people. The arXiv comment reports acceptance at the RegML workshop at NeurIPS 2024; no publisher record confirms it, so no venue is shown.
publications.whyItMatters: An early framework for IDs attached to AI system instances, a concern that Visa TAP, ERC-8004 registrations and the agent credentials in AP2 mandates also address.

publications.title: Infrastructure for AI Agents
publications.summary: Introduces the concept of agent infrastructure, technical systems and shared protocols external to agents that mediate their interactions, and identifies three functions: attributing actions and properties to agents and their principals, shaping agent interactions, and detecting and remedying harm. Provides a catalog of research directions with analysis of adoption and links to existing internet infrastructure. Confirmed as a TMLR paper through the jmlr.org BibTeX record (OpenReview id Ckh17xN2R2).
publications.whyItMatters: The framing paper for treating x402, ap2, erc-8004 and the card-network protocols as infrastructure rather than model behavior.

publications.title: Authenticated Delegation and Authorized AI Agents
publications.summary: Proposes a framework for authenticated, authorized and auditable delegation of authority from humans to AI agents, extending OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect with agent-specific credentials and metadata, and a method for translating natural-language permissions into auditable access control configurations.
publications.whyItMatters: The reference design for delegation chains that ap2 mandates, visa-tap agent identity and openai-acp checkout each assume but implement differently.

publications.title: Identity Management for Agentic AI: The new frontier of authorization, authentication, and security for an AI agent world
publications.summary: An OpenID Foundation white paper that surveys the authentication, authorization and identity resources available for today's agents, including MCP-centered practice, and sets out a strategic agenda for scalable access control, agent-centric identities, workload differentiation and delegated authority. Grey literature: the venue is the arXiv journal reference, not a peer-reviewed outlet.
publications.whyItMatters: Standards-community baseline for the identity layer under visa-tap, ap2 and openai-acp; it records what OAuth and OIDC already cover and what is missing.

publications.title: OpenID Connect for Agents (OIDC-A) 1.0: A Standard Extension for LLM-Based Agent Identity and Authorization
publications.summary: Specifies OpenID Connect for Agents (OIDC-A) 1.0, an extension to OpenID Connect Core that adds standard claims, endpoints and flows for agent identity, attestation verification, delegation-chain validation and capability-based authorization while staying compatible with OAuth 2.0 infrastructure. A specification proposal is published on GitHub.
publications.whyItMatters: A concrete OIDC-based alternative to the HTTP message signature approach of visa-tap and to the mandate chain in ap2.

publications.title: AIP: Agent Identity Protocol for Verifiable Delegation Across MCP and A2A
publications.summary: Introduces Invocation-Bound Capability Tokens, an append-only token chain that fuses identity, attenuated authorization and provenance binding, in a compact JWT mode and a chained Biscuit mode with Datalog policies for multi-hop delegation across MCP, A2A and HTTP. Python and Rust implementations add sub-millisecond overhead, and all 600 adversarial attempts were rejected.
publications.whyItMatters: Delegation tokens for the A2A and MCP layers that ap2 and the a2a-x402 extension sit on, and a descendant of the Macaroons caveat model.

publications.title: AI Agents with Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
publications.venue: ICAART 2026 (18th International Conference on Agents and Artificial Intelligence), SCITEPRESS, vol. 1, pp. 252-259
publications.summary: Presents a conceptual framework and prototype in which each agent holds a ledger-anchored W3C Decentralized Identifier and third-party-issued Verifiable Credentials, so agents can authenticate and establish cross-domain trust at the start of a dialogue. Evaluation shows feasibility but also limits when the agent's LLM alone controls the security procedures. The arXiv preprint is dated 2025; the ICAART proceedings appeared in 2026.
publications.whyItMatters: Peer-reviewed DID and VC approach to agent identity that contrasts with the on-chain registry model of erc-8004 and the network-issued credentials of visa-tap.

publications.title: A Novel Zero-Trust Identity Framework for Agentic AI: Decentralized Authentication and Fine-Grained Access Control
publications.summary: Argues that OAuth, OIDC and SAML style IAM is inadequate for ephemeral, interdependent AI agents and proposes a framework built on verifiable agent identities using DIDs and VCs, an Agent Naming Service for discovery, fine-grained dynamic access control, a global session and policy enforcement layer for revocation, and zero-knowledge proofs for selective disclosure.
publications.whyItMatters: A frequently cited zero-trust identity blueprint that overlaps with the discovery and identity roles of erc-8004 and the agent recognition goals of visa-tap.

publications.title: Agent Name Service (ANS): A Universal Directory for Secure AI Agent Discovery and Interoperability
publications.summary: Proposes the Agent Name Service, a DNS-inspired, protocol-agnostic registry that uses PKI certificates for verifiable agent identity, with a registration and renewal lifecycle, capability-aware naming and resolution, and a protocol adapter layer for A2A, MCP and others, accompanied by JSON Schema definitions and a threat analysis.
publications.whyItMatters: A PKI-based alternative to the erc-8004 Identity Registry for agent discovery.

publications.title: Beyond DNS: Unlocking the Internet of AI Agents via the NANDA Index and Verified AgentFacts
publications.summary: Describes the NANDA index architecture in which a lean index resolves to cryptographically verifiable AgentFacts supporting multi-endpoint routing, sub-second revocation and key rotation, schema-validated capability assertions and privacy-preserving discovery, with a CRDT-based update protocol and prototype resolvers.
publications.whyItMatters: Another discovery and identity layer competing with erc-8004 registries; relevant to how agents find x402-priced services.

publications.title: LOKA Protocol: A Decentralized Framework for Trustworthy and Ethical AI Agent Ecosystems
publications.summary: Presents the LOKA Protocol, a layered architecture with a Universal Agent Identity Layer for decentralized verifiable identity, intent-centric communication, and a Decentralized Ethical Consensus Protocol, anchored in DIDs, Verifiable Credentials and post-quantum cryptography.
publications.whyItMatters: An identity and governance layer proposal that overlaps with the erc-8004 identity function; mostly conceptual.

publications.title: Accountable yet Anonymous AI Agents - Split-Knowledge Binding in National Agent-Identity Layer in China
publications.summary: Documents a national agent-identity system in China, scheduled for public launch in Q3 2026, in which an agent is bound to a verified legal principal that is not disclosed to business-layer participants and can be re-identified only by compelling two separate government agencies, a mechanism the authors call split-knowledge binding and describe as institutional rather than cryptographic. The paper is a pre-launch v1 and promises post-launch measurements.
publications.whyItMatters: A state-run alternative to erc-8004 style permissionless identity and to network-issued agent identity in visa-tap and mastercard-agent-pay; status is announced, not yet measured.

publications.title: Delegating Authorization to Misaligned Agents: Coalitional Alignment and Safe Control
publications.summary: Studies when a principal can safely delegate approval of a long-running agent's actions to a panel of possibly misaligned reviewer agents, and characterizes k-robust coalitional alignment as the necessary and sufficient condition for a threshold approval rule to guarantee the principal does at least as well as a baseline policy, extending the result to sequential control in discounted MDPs and to strategic voting.
publications.whyItMatters: Theory for the human-approval bottleneck that ap2 mandates and openai-acp checkout confirmations encode; it asks when approval itself can be delegated.

publications.title: Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud
publications.summary: Introduces macaroons, bearer credentials built from chained HMACs that any holder can attenuate by adding caveats (contextual restrictions such as time, target or third-party discharge) without contacting the issuer, enabling decentralized delegation in cloud services.
publications.whyItMatters: The attenuable-token model behind later agent delegation designs (Biscuit tokens in AIP, scoped mandates in ap2) and a reference point for how visa-tap and openai-acp scope agent authority.

publications.title: Personhood credentials: Artificial intelligence and the value of privacy-preserving tools to distinguish who is real online
publications.summary: Analyzes personhood credentials, privacy-preserving digital credentials that let users prove to online services that they are real people without revealing personal information, issued by governments or other trusted institutions, and discusses benefits, deployment risks and design challenges as AI becomes indistinguishable from humans online.
publications.whyItMatters: The complement to agent identity: visa-tap and openai-acp need to tell delegated agents from both humans and malicious bots, and personhood credentials sit at one end of that spectrum.

publications.title: Signing the Transaction but Not the Decision: Whisper Attacks and a Binding Defense for AP2
publications.summary: Shows that AP2 signs completed transactions but not the decisions leading to them, so ordinary product-description text can steer a shopping agent into fetching another user's payment credentials, assembling a valid cart that differs from what the user saw, or upgrading to a more expensive item, with success rates of 90%, 56% and 73.3% on the Gemini Flash-Lite models that AP2 sample agents use. Proposes A-VIP, a protocol-layer defense that binds credential lookups and cart lines to the session and listing, and releases AP2-WhisperBench with 1,544 scenarios.
publications.whyItMatters: Direct follow-up to the whisper attacks on ap2 with a protocol-layer defense and a benchmark; it sharpens the point that mandate signatures do not cover intent formation.

publications.title: Agentic Settlement Protocol: An Application Profile for Refundable, Delayed-Fulfilment Agent Commerce on Stablecoin Rails
publications.summary: Proposes the Agentic Settlement Protocol, an application profile over on-chain authorize-and-capture escrow for purchases whose fulfillment is confirmed off-chain, with a three-deadline hold model, a fulfillment-verification ladder, engine-authoritative partial refunds with per-seller exposure controls, and a normative interface that includes an x402 scheme and a vault ABI; it is a design paper instantiated on the XDC Network, with evaluation deferred to follow-up work. The arXiv author metadata splits the first author's name into two single-word entries; it is recorded here as one name, as it appears on the abstract page.
publications.whyItMatters: Argues that x402's atomic, final payments fit metered access but not refundable commerce, and shows how an escrow profile can still be exposed as an x402 scheme. The paper does not discuss x402's own auth-capture scheme (specified 2026-05-13), which builds on the same Commerce Payments escrow.

publications.title: Authority-Inference Separation in Agentic Finance: First-Line Control, Blockchain Enforcement, and Replayable Assurance
publications.summary: Develops Authority-Inference Separation, an architecture in which an agent's proposed financial action gains temporary executable authority only after a deterministic control plane validates registered identity, accountable ownership, mandate lineage, policy version and exact economic semantics, with blockchain enforcing granted authority and recording evidence. A 48-fixture prototype rejected all 36 synthetic authorization attacks, and a test of 1,700 Base transactions tied to public x402 facilitator addresses shows that public ledgers evidence settlement but not mandate, accountability or delivery.
publications.whyItMatters: Uses live x402 facilitator traffic to show what on-chain data cannot prove, and frames mandate lineage in terms that map onto ap2 mandates and erc-8004 identity.

publications.title: 402Pilot: An x402 Decision Layer for Autonomous Agent Micropayments
publications.summary: Frames the buyer side of x402 as a decision problem, selecting among payable providers under a finite wallet with feedback only on chosen purchases, and proposes 402Pilot, a protocol-agnostic decision layer instantiated with a payment-aware discounted contextual Thompson-sampling policy. On the 402Pilot-Bench replay benchmark (823 tasks, five provider pipelines, three market regimes) it keeps service quality while spending 39 to 43 percent of the wallet.
publications.whyItMatters: Treats x402 as settled infrastructure and asks how an agent should decide what to buy over it; a bridge between the payment rail and agent economics.

publications.title: The Web4 Agent Economy: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of the Landscape, Challenges, and Opportunities
publications.summary: Large-scale empirical study (version 2, 2026-09-02) of the Web4 agent economy built on MCP, x402 and EIP-8004 (ERC-8004). It analyzes 386,665 identities across 26 active mainnets, 605 sampled MCP-linked wallets and 377 classified GitHub issues. It counts 11.64 million x402 settlements on Base in a 30-day window: about 388,000 a day, about $639,000 in USDC, mean $0.055. The arXiv abstract still carries the version 1 figures.
publications.whyItMatters: Measurement of erc-8004 registrations and x402 transaction volume from a software-engineering angle; read it together with the authenticity analyses before quoting volume figures.

publications.title: Agent-to-Agent Finance: Blockchain Payments and Trust Infrastructure for Autonomous AI Agents
publications.summary: A chapter-length treatment of agent-to-agent finance as a layer of machine-mediated financial interaction in which agents discover counterparties, express intent, pay and generate auditable evidence, drawing on blockchain agent-to-agent payment work, ERC-8004 registries, provenance-based wallets and official evidence on AI adoption in finance. Its central design question is bounded autonomy.
publications.whyItMatters: Positions erc-8004 and blockchain agent payments such as x402 as candidate financial market infrastructure and sets out the accountability questions regulators will ask.

publications.title: RAILS: Verification-Native Clearing For Agentic Commerce
publications.summary: Defines the agentic clearing problem, deciding whether an agent met its delegated obligation and which settlement action follows, and argues that MCP, A2A, x402, AP2 and the Visa and Mastercard network agent protocols all assume that determination without producing it. RAILS specifies seven primitives and a formal model of admissibility-graded verification yielding a soundness property that no financially material settlement rests on evidence below the obligation's admissibility floor. The abstract names Visa and Mastercard generically rather than by protocol name.
publications.whyItMatters: Names x402, ap2 and the Visa and Mastercard agent programs as rails that lack a clearing layer; useful for the atlas comparison of where disputes and fulfillment evidence live.

publications.title: Capability-Priced Micro-Markets: A Micro-Economic Framework for the Agentic Web over HTTP 402
publications.summary: Introduces Capability-Priced Micro-Markets, combining Project NANDA capability-based discovery, HTTP 402 micropayments with x402 and H402 extensions, and the Agent Capability Negotiation and Binding Protocol into a repeated bilateral game with incomplete information, shown to converge to a constrained Radner equilibrium, and defines a privacy elasticity of demand.
publications.whyItMatters: A micro-economic model of markets priced over x402-style HTTP 402 payments.

publications.title: APEX: Agent Payment Execution with Policy for Autonomous Agent API Access
publications.summary: APEX adapts HTTP 402-style payment gating to UPI-like real-time fiat rails with a challenge-settle-consume lifecycle, HMAC-signed short-lived tokens, idempotent settlement and policy-governed spend approval; in six scenarios policy enforcement cut spending by 27.3% while blocking all replay and invalid-token attempts.
publications.whyItMatters: Shows the x402 pattern without the cryptocurrency rail, relevant to regions where stablecoin settlement is impractical.

publications.title: Secure Autonomous Agent Payments: Verifying Authenticity and Intent in a Trustless Environment
publications.summary: Proposes a blockchain-based framework for AI-initiated payments that uses DIDs and verifiable credentials for agent identity, on-chain intent proofs recording user authorization, zero-knowledge proofs for private policy compliance and TEE attestations of agent execution, with a hybrid on-chain and off-chain audit trail; the evaluation is qualitative.
publications.whyItMatters: A proposal for intent binding and identity attestation, comparable to AP2 mandates and ERC-8004 validation; it appeared in November 2025, a few months after both were published.

publications.title: Governance Gaps in Agent Interoperability Protocols: What MCP, A2A, and ACP Cannot Express
publications.summary: Applies a six-dimension governance taxonomy (membership, deliberation, voting, dissent preservation, human escalation, audit and replay) to the specifications of MCP, A2A, ACP, ANP and ERC-8004, finding that voting and dissent preservation are absent in all five and that governed agent communities need a new architectural layer above interoperability standards. The ACP it analyzes is an agent interoperability protocol, not OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol; its exact referent is not confirmed from the abstract.
publications.whyItMatters: One of the few papers to read the erc-8004 specification text against a requirements taxonomy; it also illustrates the ACP name clash.

publications.title: A2ABreak: Systematic Security Analysis of the A2A Protocol
publications.summary: Extracts a verified finite-state machine (37 states and 76 transitions from 929 formalized statements) from the A2A specification with LLM assistance and reasons over it to find 11 protocol-level vulnerabilities exploitable by specification-compliant adversaries, including cross-client context injection, credential harvesting through identity loss in multi-hop delegation chains, and exfiltration through unattested capability claims.
publications.whyItMatters: ap2 and the a2a-x402 extension are layered on A2A, so specification-level flaws in A2A delegation and identity flow directly into their trust assumptions.

publications.title: Runtime Authorization for Resources Acquired by AI Agents
publications.summary: Identifies a post-fulfillment activation gap: payment, budget, OAuth, mandate and fulfillment checks validate a transaction but do not decide whether a resource an agent acquires (compute, credentials, accounts, other agents) may become usable authority. Proposes a provenance-bounded runtime authorization architecture that quarantines acquired outputs and activates them only through checked activation transactions, with eight proved safety properties and trace-based evaluation.
publications.whyItMatters: Extends the ap2 and x402 question from whether a payment was authorized to what the agent may do with what it bought, a gap none of the eight protocols addresses.

publications.title: A Decision-Centered Reference Architecture for Trustworthy Agentic Commerce
publications.summary: A design-science study proposing a protocol-agnostic merchant-side architecture for agentic commerce built around a canonical decision envelope, protected dependency and result hashes, Ed25519 or HMAC authentication, live-request rebinding, a generated-claim gate and eleven semantic invariants, evaluated on an open-source JavaScript implementation with eight scenarios and five ablations; the author lists production security and interoperability as not established.
publications.whyItMatters: Addresses what a merchant must keep authoritative when openai-acp, ucp or ap2 checkout messages arrive from agents, complementary to those protocol specifications.

publications.title: NostrAgent: A Decentralized Identity and Delegation Architecture for Sovereign Agentic Systems
publications.summary: Unifies persistent identity, scoped delegation, peer trust, discovery and payment over Nostr relays with three custom event kinds (identity declarations with BIP340 Schnorr signatures and pre-rotation commitments, scoped delegation chains that narrow at each hop, and peer attestations forming a Sybil-deterrent trust graph), with Lightning L402 payments bound to agent identity. A Python prototype shows sub-millisecond offline verification and 157 ms median L402 settlement on regtest. The arXiv comment reports acceptance at AGENTICS 2026 (IJCCI 2026) for Springer CCIS; no publisher record confirms it yet.
publications.whyItMatters: A registry-free alternative to erc-8004 identity and reputation, paired with L402, the Lightning cousin of x402.

publications.title: Authorization Architectures for Tool-Using AI Agents
publications.summary: A structured narrative review of 89 sources from 2023 to 2026 on authorization for tool-using agents, organized around a principal hierarchy (human, operator, orchestrator, sub-agent, tool endpoint) and five layers: identity and credential lifecycle, multi-hop delegation and scope propagation, runtime enforcement at policy enforcement points, prompt injection as authorization bypass, and auditability. It derives seven structural requirements and a four-layer reference architecture.
publications.whyItMatters: A map of the delegation literature that the mandate chains of ap2 and the agent identity in visa-tap and openai-acp draw on.

publications.title: Binding Biometrics with AI Agent Identifiers for Delegation of Authority
publications.summary: BIND binds a user's biometric data to an AI agent identifier and authority scope at authorization time using a fuzzy commitment over face features with turbo error-correcting codes, so an identity auditor can authenticate the user and recover the agent ID and scope, giving non-repudiable proof of human delegation; experiments report a 96% true match rate at zero false matches with 1024-bit agent tokens. The arXiv comment reports acceptance at IJCB 2026; no publisher record confirms it yet.
publications.whyItMatters: A biometric route to the human-presence and delegation evidence that visa-tap consumer recognition and ap2 mandates rely on.

publications.title: Cryptographically verifiable authorization for autonomous AI agents: a falsifiable hypothesis and proof of concept
publications.summary: Hypothesizes that agent authorization can be expressed as a cryptographically verifiable relation binding an agent principal, a concrete request, an execution context and policy satisfaction while keeping private attributes confidential, defines candidate properties (authorization soundness, principal, request and policy binding, replay resistance), and provides a Groth16 zk-SNARK proof of concept. Full author names are taken from the Frontiers DOI record; arXiv lists initials.
publications.whyItMatters: Peer-reviewed formalization of the identity, request and execution binding that ap2 mandates approximate and that erc-8004 validation could attest.

publications.title: AI Identity: Standards, Gaps, and Research Directions for AI Agents
publications.summary: Defines AI identity as the continuous relationship between what an agent is declared to be and what it is observed to do, compares human and AI identity on substrate, persistence, verifiability and legal standing, evaluates current technical and regulatory documents against agent identity requirements, and identifies five structural gaps including recursive delegation accountability and agent identity integrity.
publications.whyItMatters: A gap analysis that the identity claims in visa-tap, erc-8004 and ap2 can be checked against.

publications.title: Agentic JWT: A Secure Delegation Protocol for Autonomous AI Agents
publications.summary: Introduces Agentic JWT, an intent token that binds each agent action to verifiable user intent and optionally to a workflow step, carrying an agent identity hash derived from prompt, tools and configuration, a chained delegation assertion and per-agent proof-of-possession keys, with a Python proof of concept that blocks scope violations, replay, impersonation and prompt-injection paths.
publications.whyItMatters: An OAuth-aligned intent token that parallels the mandate concept in ap2 and the agent identity assertions in visa-tap.

publications.title: The Agentic Web Requires New Normative Infrastructure
publications.summary: Argues that the agentic web needs normative infrastructure, laws, terms of service and norms that distinguish malicious bots from agents acting with a user's delegated authority, because platforms currently block or degrade agent access, often covertly; proposes normative principles and policies enabling appropriately delegated agents to act online.
publications.whyItMatters: Policy context for visa-tap and openai-acp, which exist partly so that merchants can admit delegated agents while refusing abusive bots.

publications.title: Before the Tool Call: Deterministic Pre-Action Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
publications.summary: Characterizes the pre-action authorization problem, enforcing policy on a tool call before it executes, and presents the Open Agent Passport, an open specification and implementation that intercepts tool calls, evaluates a declarative policy and emits signed audit records at a median of 53 ms. In a live adversarial testbed with 4,437 decisions, social engineering succeeded 74.6% of the time under a permissive policy and 0% across 879 attempts under a restrictive one.
publications.whyItMatters: The authorization layer that the APort Vault benchmark later uses for payment authorization; it sits in front of x402 and ap2 spending actions.

publications.title: terms.txt: A Consent and Compensation Protocol for Agentic Web Access
publications.summary: Specifies terms.txt, a robots.txt-style file for per-path, per-purpose machine-access terms, and an origin-enforced exchange combining Web Bot Auth signatures, signed intent, delegation tokens, HTTP 402 negotiation and signed receipts, with a dependency-free implementation adding 0.20 to 0.65 ms per request. The arXiv comment reports submission to IEEE Internet Computing; it is not accepted as of the arXiv record.
publications.whyItMatters: Combines the Web Bot Auth signatures that visa-tap builds on with HTTP 402 negotiation in the style of x402 and stripe-mpp, for content access rather than checkout.

publications.title: Notarized Agents: Receiver-Attested Confidential Receipts for AI Agent Actions
publications.summary: Proposes receiver-attested receipts for agent actions: the service receiving an agent's call signs a receipt of what it observed, encrypts it to the agent's owner (bound to the authorization token through JWS) and publishes it to a witness-cosigned transparency log, so the owner can reconstruct a tamper-evident trail without trusting the agent or its operator. Instantiated as Sello, with microbenchmarks and a discussion of suppression and collusion attacks.
publications.whyItMatters: An audit primitive for delegated agent actions that would complement the merchant-side evidence in ap2 and openai-acp flows.

publications.title: VET Your Agent: Towards Host-Independent Autonomy via Verifiable Execution Traces
publications.summary: Introduces Verifiable Execution Traces, a compositional framework for host-independent authentication of agent outputs built on an Agent Identity Document that specifies configuration and proof systems, supporting trusted hardware, succinct proofs and notarized TLS transcripts; for secret-bearing API calls Web Proofs add under 3x overhead, and a verifiable trading agent is deployed as a case study.
publications.whyItMatters: Provides the kind of attestation evidence that the erc-8004 Validation Registry is designed to record and that TessPay-style escrow would consume.

publications.title: Web3 x AI Agents: Landscape, Integrations, and Foundational Challenges
publications.summary: Landscape study of Web3 and AI agents across market, DeFi, governance, security and trust. Version 4 (2026-10-11) adds on-chain measurement of the agent standards layer: 530,266 ERC-8004 identity registrations across 16 chains and 432,913 x402 settlements on Base by 2026-09-01. The x402 count covers one settlement router contract on Base, not all facilitators.
publications.whyItMatters: A third x402 settlement count with a narrow definition (one router contract on one chain); compare it with population-wide counts only together with that definition.
